body:
Tested this PR a bit.

1. Disabling Auto Font Size doesn't revert the font size back to the default.

2. In my opinion, Min and Max should be spelled out as Minimum and Maximum in the inspector, for accessibility reasons.

3. When Minimum Font Size > Maximum Font Size, the minimum font size takes precedent. I guess either way is fine, but I expected the opposite. Should be documented in each property's description.

4. For all the nodes that also have an associated icon or other control that is not technically a font (Button, CheckBox, and CheckButton), I think this implementation is not going to fly. IMO either we strip those node types out of this PR (which I think I'd prefer), or this PR introduces more specialized controls that help manage the icon / addition control sizes in a more encompassing way. I think this PR would stand a higher chance of being merged if it just focussed on Label and RichTextLabel initially, and introduce auto font sizing on other nodes should there be sufficient requests and a more specific proposal that also addresses how icons and other controls part of the parent control should be managed.

Tested this PR. It works as expected and looks good to me overall. Two nitpicky suggestions:
- Integrate the enable checkbox as described above.
- I'm a _bit_ bothered by the name 'Auto Font Size' and would rather name this to include the word 'fit', I think? How about… `Resize Font to Fit`?

Tested this a lot more and found two bugs:

- On a Label, when `Resize Font to Fit` is enabled and `Autowrap Mode` is set to `Word (Smart)`, the Control can be resized to smaller than the minimum height of the Label making the text disappear entirely – whereas, if `Resize Font to Fit` is disabled, the height can never be smaller than the font height.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b9cb2e3-11fe-4300-9ab3-cf439f040550

We should retain the original behavior; text should always be visible, so minimum height should always be enforced.

- On a RichTextLabel, if you have both `Fit Content` and `Resize Font to Fit` enabled, you can only grow the Control but never shrink it.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/899ea7e0-0b9a-4e30-bba2-34521658e651

The expected behavior is that you are able to shrink it to the point where the minimum size is achieved.

- Other than that, works great.

Tested locally (rebased on top of `master` 06c3946e3501a7f52a10eed96d200b93df17d373), it mostly works as expected. Code looks good to me. Example on the [RichTextLabel demo](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/gui/rich_text_bbcode): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c205f51f-0e25-458a-91c9-06282b15d531 Some feedback: - Dropcap (the yellow `F`) and list bullets do not automatically resize, unlike font sizes overridden with `font_size` (which are scaled relative to the theme font size, e.g. `24` is 150% of the default `16`). I consider this a bug, so it'd be good to fix if possible. List bullets in the table as seen below with a small automatic font size: - If floating-point font sizes were supported, fonts could rescale more smoothly and take the full horizontal space of the label more optimally, especially at low font sizes. See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/87243.

This works fine with simple embedded images using the new `em` tag

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e327ab8d-c90b-4b9d-8ba6-5e140b1cb24b

But fails once you combine the new `em` and existing `font_size` tag, as you can see in the video below, the 2D icon in the large text only scales up to the `maximum_font_size` instead of scaling up to `maximum_font_size * p_base_font_size / theme_cache.normal_font_size`

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c77b31cf-5c1f-4e8e-a688-ed3629085cd2

You probably need to touch these two lines that were added by #112617:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1aabcb9e9bc7a222a972731523831ec86b77ee20/scene/gui/rich_text_label.cpp#L563
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1aabcb9e9bc7a222a972731523831ec86b77ee20/scene/gui/rich_text_label.cpp#L788

LGTM!

Issue fixed, and this works beautifully. I have not looked at code quality.

Code looks good. Seems to work as expected.

Needs rebase (minor `Label::get_minimum_size` changes).
